title: Verity Valley Power & Light - News & Announcements
description: Corporate announcements from Verity Valley Power & Light. Posted when there is an announcement, which is not often. Comments are not enabled.

data.author: Corporate Communications
data.tagline: News and announcements for our customers and the communities we serve.
data.about:
Verity Valley Power & Light provides electric service to approximately 41,000 customers in Verity County and adjacent areas.

This page carries company announcements, service updates and planned work notices. It is not monitored for service requests. To report an outage or a downed line, contact Customer Care or call 911.

Comments are not enabled on this page.

[b]Media inquiries:[/b] Corporate Communications.

posts.title: Verity Valley Power & Light Announces Service Center Improvements
posts.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light today announced improvements to the way customers in Verity County access account services.

Effective 1 May 2019, the walk-in payment window at the Gridfall service center on Depot Street will close. Customers may continue to pay by mail, by telephone, online, or in person at participating retail payment locations throughout the service territory.

"These improvements reflect how our customers have told us they prefer to do business with us," the company said in a statement.

The Gridfall service center has served customers at its Depot Street location since 1951. The building will be retained for equipment storage.

Customers who have historically used the walk-in window will receive a notice with their next statement. The notice includes a list of participating retail payment locations. The list is also available through the company's online account portal at [url=synth://vvplconnect.synth/]vvplconnect[/url].

Customer Care is available Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., and is the appropriate point of contact for questions regarding billing, payment arrangements and service requests.

Verity Valley Power & Light is committed to providing safe, reliable service to the communities it serves.

Media Contact: D. Hovey, Corporate Communications

posts.title: Planned Maintenance Activity at Substation No. 3
posts.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light will perform planned maintenance activity at Substation No. 3 in Gridfall beginning the week of 21 September 2020.

The work forms part of the company's ongoing inspection cycle and will be carried out by a contracted crew. Customers in portions of Gridfall and Tannery Flats may experience brief service interruptions of up to fifteen minutes during the work window. Interruptions are not anticipated outside the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.

No action is required by customers. Customers with medical equipment requiring continuous power should contact Customer Care to review their account designation.

Substation No. 3 was rebuilt in 2015 and is a modern, fully automated facility monitored continuously from Verity Valley's regional operations center.

We appreciate our customers' patience while this work is completed. Planned maintenance activity is an important part of a commitment to reliability.

Media Contact: D. Hovey, Corporate Communications

posts.title: Verity Valley Files Rate Adjustment Reflecting Infrastructure Investment
posts.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light has filed with the state utility commission for a rate adjustment reflecting infrastructure investment made across its service territory since 2015.

If approved as filed, the adjustment would take effect 1 January 2022. A residential customer using 900 kilowatt-hours per month would see a change of approximately $6.40 per month.

The filing supports continued investment in automation, remote monitoring and system hardening, including work completed at Substation No. 3 and at four other facilities in the region. Investment of this kind is not visible to most customers on most days, which is precisely the intention.

The company recognizes that any adjustment affects household budgets. Assistance programs are available to qualifying customers, and customers experiencing difficulty are encouraged to contact Customer Care before a balance becomes past due.

The commission's review process includes a period for public comment. Details of that process are published by the commission.

Verity Valley Power & Light remains committed to safe, reliable and affordable service for the communities it serves.

Media Contact: D. Hovey, Corporate Communications

[i]Updated 4 January 2022: the adjustment described above was approved and took effect as filed.[/i]

posts.title: Supporting the Communities We Serve
posts.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light supported a number of community organizations and programs across its service territory during 2021.

Contributions included support for the Verity County Fair, a scholarship awarded to a graduating senior pursuing a career in the skilled trades, and sponsorship of a safety education program delivered in area schools.

"Being part of the communities we serve is important to us," the company said.

Total community giving across the service territory in 2021 was $14,200. This included $250 in direct support of the Verity County Fair.

Employees also participated in volunteer activities in several communities during the year.

Verity Valley Power & Light thanks the organizations that made these partnerships possible. Organizations seeking support may submit a request through Corporate Communications. Requests are reviewed annually.

Media Contact: D. Hovey, Corporate Communications

posts.title: Twenty Years On: Learning From Our History
posts.body:
Twenty years ago today, on 11 June 2003, a fire occurred at Substation No. 3 in Gridfall.

The event affected approximately 4,100 customers, some of them for several days. Two volunteer firefighters were treated and released. Crews and mutual aid partners worked around the clock to restore service to the affected area.

An anniversary is an opportunity to reflect. At Verity Valley Power & Light, we believe that learning from our history is an essential part of a culture of safety. Every event we experience informs the way we plan, build and operate the system our customers depend on.

In the years since 2003, Verity Valley has made significant investment in the reliability of its infrastructure across the region. Equipment has been replaced. Monitoring has been modernized. Inspection cycles have been reviewed and, where appropriate, revised. Substation No. 3 itself was rebuilt in 2015 to current standards, with automation and remote monitoring capabilities that did not exist in 2003.

We are also mindful that a system is more than its equipment. Our people, our training and our processes are what turn investment into reliability. Verity Valley's safety culture is grounded in the principle that every employee and every contractor has both the right and the responsibility to raise a concern.

Looking forward, the company will continue to invest in the systems and technologies that support reliability throughout its service territory. Grid modernization work now underway will further improve Verity Valley's ability to detect, isolate and respond to conditions on the system. Customers will see the benefit of this work in the form of fewer interruptions and shorter restoration times.

The company continues to work closely with state regulators, with local emergency management, and with the communities it serves. Verity Valley representatives are available to speak with community organizations on request.

We are grateful to the first responders who answered that morning, to the crews who restored service, and to our customers for their patience during a difficult week.

Reliability is measured one customer at a time. Two decades is a long time. The system has changed. The commitment has not.

Questions regarding the 2003 event may be directed to Corporate Communications.

Media Contact: Corporate Communications

posts.title: Storm Restoration Update
posts.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light crews continue to restore service following the winter weather system that moved through the region beginning Sunday evening.

At the peak of the event, approximately 1,880 customers were without service across Verity County and adjacent areas. As of 6:00 a.m. Tuesday, that number stands at 215.

Restoration is being carried out by company crews and by contract crews mobilized from outside the affected area. Restoration times in some locations reflect travel distance and road conditions. We appreciate our customers' patience.

Customers should treat every downed line as energized and should not approach it. Downed lines should be reported to Customer Care or to 911.

Estimated restoration times are updated as damage assessment is completed and are available through the company's online account portal at [url=synth://vvplconnect.synth/]vvplconnect[/url].

County road conditions and emergency information are published by Verity County at [url=synth://verity.county.gov/]verity.county.gov[/url]. Current regional conditions are also available on the county dashboard at [url=synth://dash.verity.net/]dash.verity.net[/url].

Verity Valley Power & Light thanks the crews working in difficult conditions and the communities supporting them.

Media Contact: Corporate Communications

posts.title: Verity Valley Completes Grid Modernization Milestone
posts.body:
Verity Valley Power & Light has completed installation of advanced metering infrastructure across its Verity County service area.

The project, which began in 2023, replaced legacy meters at approximately 41,000 service locations. Advanced meters report consumption and outage information automatically, reducing the need for on-site visits and enabling the company's regional operations center to detect and confirm an interruption without a customer call.

Customers are not required to take any action. Meter readings appear on statements as before. Customers who wish to review interval consumption data may do so through the company's online account portal at [url=synth://vvplconnect.synth/]vvplconnect[/url].

Verity Valley Power & Light was recognized this year for reliability performance in a regional benchmarking study.

"This milestone reflects a commitment to reliability and to the communities we serve," the company said.

Work continues on the remaining phases of the company's grid modernization program.

Media Contact: Corporate Communications
